Location: Western Florida Panhandle – Pensacola, Destin, Panama City, Port St. Joe and the GIWW (miles 167–376)
Item: Hurricane Isaias aftermath – Panhandle ports and GIWW in Coast Guard 'recovery' status
Details: Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin around 8:30pm CDT Fri Oct 9 as a Category 2 (105 mph); Panama City saw about 5.5 ft of storm surge. In the Coast Guard Sector Mobile update reported Oct 12, Pensacola, Destin, Panama City, Port St. Joe and GIWW miles 167–376 were in 'recovery' status: commercial traffic suspended and recreational vessels 65 ft and over restricted until channel surveys are done (GIWW miles 44.5–166 normal). Destin Marina and Dewey Destin's were reported badly damaged; FWC has been tagging derelict vessels in Santa Rosa, Okaloosa and Walton counties, and locals report logs and debris in the water. Why it matters: even where boats under 65 ft can move, channels haven't all been surveyed, marks may be off station and debris is floating – this is not the week for a night passage or an assumed fuel/slip stop in Destin.
When: Since Oct 9 2026; recovery status – end not announced
Notes: What to do: before moving a boat along the Panhandle, check navcen.uscg.gov/port-status (zone Mobile) and Sector Mobile's latest MSIB (the Oct 12 port-status page points to MSIB 136-26, which I could not read), or call the Sector Mobile Command Center at 251-266-5888 / VHF 16. Call ahead to any Destin-area marina before counting on a slip or fuel. Travel in daylight with a sharp bow lookout. Uncertainty: the NavCen page shows Pensacola and Panama City 'Open' as of Oct 12 (see Route Open row), but Destin and the GIWW miles 167–376 status after Oct 12 is not confirmed. My reading is that GIWW miles 167–376 (miles east of Harvey Lock) runs roughly from the Pensacola area to the end of the GIWW in the Big Bend – check your chart. Fall Pensacola Bay regattas already in the sheet (Jubilee Regatta Oct 31–Nov 1) may be affected – confirm with the club. Map point: Destin.

Location: Dog River / Dog River Inlet near the Dog River Bridge, Mobile (west side of Mobile Bay)
Item: Pier debris in Dog River inlet after Isaias
Details: Coast Guard MSIB 126-26 (Oct 10): a roughly 20-ft section of pier broke loose near Dog River Marina during the storm, drifted toward the Dog River Bridge inlet and has been breaking apart in or near the inlet. Why it matters: Dog River is a popular stop for cruisers on the west side of Mobile Bay, and broken dock sections can float just at the surface – easy to hit with a keel or prop in a narrow inlet.
When: Posted Oct 10 2026; until cleared (no end date given)
Notes: What to do: transit Dog River at slow speed with a lookout on the bow, and report debris or unsafe conditions to Coast Guard Sector Mobile Command Center 251-266-5888 (Waterways Management 251-382-8653). No coordinates in the notice; map point is approximate (Dog River Bridge).

Location: Ports of Mobile, Gulfport, Pascagoula, Pensacola and Panama City (Coast Guard Sector Mobile)
Item: Mobile-area ports reopened after Hurricane Isaias
Details: The Port of Mobile returned to port condition normal at 4pm Sat Oct 10; Gulfport and Pascagoula are back to normal too. The Coast Guard's NavCen port-status page lists Gulfport, Mobile, Pascagoula, Pensacola and Panama City as 'Open' as of Oct 12, each with a note to see MSIB 136-26, and Florida reported the ports of Pensacola and Panama City reopened Mon Oct 12. Why it matters: the big harbors west of Destin are usable again – Mobile Bay and the Mississippi Sound are a reasonable place to stage while the eastern Panhandle sorts itself out.
When: Mobile normal Oct 10; Pensacola & Panama City open Oct 12 2026
Notes: What to do: read MSIB 136-26 for any leftover restrictions before departing (I could not find its text online), and call your destination marina – shore power, water and fuel may still be limited where electricity is out. Destin is not on the NavCen list and the GIWW east of Pensacola was still in 'recovery' in the last update found (see ICW Alert row). State column = AL as the main port; covers MS, AL and FL. Map point: Port of Mobile.

Location: Davis Island Yacht Club, 1315 Severn Ave, Tampa (Hillsborough Bay)
Details: Davis Island Yacht Club hosts the 2026 Star North Americans: check-in and inspection Oct 25–26, practice race Mon Oct 26, then two races a day Tue Oct 27 – Fri Oct 30 (first warning 11am), awards Friday. Why it matters: the Star is one of the great two-person keelboat classes, and a North American championship brings serious sailors to Tampa – fun to watch from the Davis Islands waterfront.
Notes: What to do: give the race area room if transiting Hillsborough Bay that week; check DIYC for spectator options (the event page doesn't mention any). Contact listed: Claude Bonanni (regatta), PRO Paul Leonard. Starts the day after DIYC's Halloween Regatta (Oct 24), already in the sheet – a big racing week in Tampa.

Location: Capt. Anderson's Marina, Grand Lagoon, Panama City Beach
Item: UPDATE: PCB Seafood Festival moved to Oct 16–18
Details: The PCB Seafood Festival, originally Oct 9–11 at Capt. Anderson's Marina, was pushed back by Hurricane Isaias and now runs Fri Oct 16 (5–9pm), Sat Oct 17 and Sun Oct 18 (11am–9pm), with fireworks over Grand Lagoon Saturday at 9pm. Free admission. Why it matters: a waterfront festival right on Grand Lagoon – easy to reach by boat for anyone who rode out the storm in Panama City.
Notes: What to do: if anchoring or docking in Grand Lagoon for the fireworks, call ahead – Panama City took about 5.5 ft of surge and some docks may be short of power or slips. Not previously in the sheet (it was rescheduled from Oct 9–11, per WJHG). Same week as Schooners' Lobster Festival on PCB (Oct 12–18, in the sheet) – its status after the storm wasn't checked. Map point approximate.
